name: Desk App
description: An entry on the dock: a named group of modules, or the stand-in for an installed app (or Other) whose place, title, mark, modules and visibility it changes. The dock lists these at their places; every module none of them claims is still reachable, grouped under the installed app it belongs to.

fields.label: Title
fields.description: What the dock's tooltip and the sidebar header call this app. Filled in from the installed app when one is picked.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: A disabled record changes nothing: it claims none of its modules, and an installed app it stands for is drawn as if it had no record. To take an app off the dock, use Hide from Dock.

fields.label: Dock Position
fields.description: Where this app sits when it is not in its default place: "top", or the key of the app it follows (app:erpnext, desk-app:Finance). Left blank, an installed app's record sits where the app would (install order, Other last), and an app of the site's own at the top. Manage Desk Apps sets this; it writes a position only for the apps that move.

fields.label: Icon
fields.description: Drawn on the dock when there is no logo. Left blank with no logo either, an installed app keeps the logo its code gives it.

fields.label: Logo
fields.description: Drawn on the dock in place of the icon.

fields.label: Color
fields.description: The app's colour on the Apps screen: its module tiles are drawn in it rather than in the colour of the app's own artwork. With no logo uploaded here, an installed app's SVG logo is redrawn in it too, on the dock and the Apps screen: its main colour is swapped for this one. A logo in any other form stays as it is; upload one here to change it.

fields.label: Modules
fields.description: The modules this app offers, in the order the dock's menus list them: drag rows to reorder. For an installed app in Add mode, these come first and the app's other modules follow in its default order: the order its shipped Dock record gives them, leaving out the ones that record hides; else Home, or the one named after the app, first, then alphabetical. Listing a module that record hides puts it back. A module can belong to only one enabled app. A Category row is a heading over the modules after it, and a Spacer row a gap; a Category left last heads the app's other modules.

fields.label: Frontend URL
fields.description: An app with a frontend of its own, outside the desk, such as /helpdesk or /commons. Offered beside the app's modules and opened in the same tab. An app with a frontend and no modules opens it straight from the dock. Left blank, an installed app keeps the frontend its code declares.

fields.label: Frontend Label
fields.description: What the module list and the top menu call the frontend. Left blank, the app's title followed by "app".

fields.label: Roles
fields.description: Only people with one of these roles see the app on the dock. Left empty, everyone does. Either way, a module a person cannot open is not offered to them.

fields.label: Installed App
fields.description: Leave blank for a grouping of your own. Pick an installed app, or Other, to change that app's entry instead: this record takes its place on the dock. An installed app Frappe does not list as somewhere to go (it declares no add_to_apps_screen, like Telephony and Print Designer) has no dock entry of its own and its modules are in Other; a record standing for it brings it back. Only one enabled record can stand for each.

fields.label: Hide from Dock
fields.description: Takes the app off the dock for everyone. Its modules go with it rather than back to an installed app; they can still be opened by address.

fields.label: Modules Mode
fields.description: Add: the app keeps the modules it already has, after any listed below. Replace: only the modules listed below, in their order; the rest go to Other, except the ones its shipped Dock record hides, which stay off the dock.

fields.label: Apps Screen
fields.options:
Default
One Icon
Icon per Module
App and Module Icons
Hidden
fields.description: How the Apps screen (/desk) shows this app, when Open Desk Settings arranges it from the Desk Apps. Default: as Frappe does, one tile if the installed app asks for one and none if it does not (Telephony and Print Designer do not); one tile for an app of your own. One Icon: a single tile, opening the app, either way. Icon per Module: a tile for each of its modules (and its frontend), in the order of its modules. App and Module Icons: the app's tile, then a tile for each of its modules. Hidden: not on the Apps screen; it stays on the dock. An app taken off the dock is off the Apps screen too.
